METHODS & LIMITS

What actually learns?

The 32-weight external value readout. The FlyWire v783 wiring stays fixed. MaleCNS and dopamine pathways are not used in this learning rule.

Artificial ORN cue → fixed LIF simulation → cached activity → value readout → left/right choice → delayed reward → readout update

Anatomy ≠ dynamics ≠ learning

flypoke supplies a Shiu-style leaky integrate-and-fire model with assumed transmitter signs and uniform neuron parameters. Python simulates the full retained graph. The browser resamples independent recorded responses; it does not simulate 139,000 neurons live.

The point layout is schematic, not anatomical. Brightness and spike counts come from saved trials. The 3D body uses simplified Flybody anatomical meshes (Apache 2.0). The walking gait and path are authored kinematics, not MuJoCo physics or a neural motor policy. The chosen destination comes from the selected controller. FlyWire brain anatomy and this body are separate sources.

Delayed reward, modest claim

There is one decision per episode, with a common horizon of delay + 1 ticks. An external buffer holds the chosen feature until payout. The learner fits the discounted Monte Carlo return: G = bonus + γdelay × money. It does not receive a target preference.

The delay control uses abstract task ticks, not biological seconds. The 250 ms LIF response window is a separate clock. The follower and reputation counts are fictional bookkeeping.

Controls & evaluation

Labels swap sides every episode; cue identities are counterbalanced across learner seeds. The shared readout scores each option, so position invariance is engineered. Test and 120 Hz transfer response seeds never occur in training. These are finite response banks sampled with replacement, not new neural trials per choice.

The random-network null permutes connection targets before duplicate coalescing; it is not an exact degree-preserving simple graph. The MLP sees raw cue identity. The frozen readout is an untrained zero-weight controller; the disconnected control has zero downstream features. Turning off cue retention prevents delayed cash from updating the readout.

No claim of novelty or superiority follows from this demo. Publishable neuroscience would require stronger topology nulls, multiple circuit selections and anatomies, physiological calibration, and preregistered biological validation.
